title: Week one of a Hugo portfolio

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Imagine you want a personal site that's just text files in git, and a web page appears when you push. That's the idea Antoine chased in the first week of moving his portfolio to Hugo, in January 2024.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So why Hugo and not a regular CMS?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Three reasons on his page. Static generation means cheap hosting, fast builds and no database to patch. Markdown sources live in git, so changes are reviewable diffs. And Hugo modules pull in a theme without copying everything into the repo. As an engineer, he wanted the repository to be the source of truth: Markdown in, HTML out.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A repository with several separate pieces: a web résumé built from JSON Resume, a PDF CV in LaTeX, two research papers, a Hugo links page and a blog theme. That's four toolchains: npm, LaTeX, Hugo and Docker.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And the links page came first?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It was his first real Hugo site. One home page, a back link layout, and two translation files for English and French. The links are a simple list in the config, and the key like github picks both the icon and the label. Tailwind builds the CSS, so plain Hugo can bundle it without extra tools.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What about the theme for the new site?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: HBTheme. It brought comments, npm-friendly assets and Hugo modules, so he didn't rebuild layouts from zero. A batteries-included theme gets you moving fast in week one.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: He embedded a Montreal car-theft data study from a friend's Substack, to prove the site could carry charts and long reads. That's where Substack fits: Hugo is the professional home, Substack is an optional channel for long essays and newsletters.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A reusable shortcode lets a post embed an HTTPS page, with a title and height. The example is an old FlashGames demo, still on GitHub Pages, now wrapped in a stable URL and the site's typography.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So where did it go next?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The site grew modules, bilingual posts and conference notes. The part two post tells that story.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A good picture of how a portfolio starts small and grows.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The full write-up has the tables and the config snippets.
